content.comment_body: Hello all, I am looking to connect a [product_name] controller to a SCADA system over the internet. The SCADA and controller are in different locations. Could you provide detailed steps for both hardware and software setup to achieve this? Thank you in advance.
If the [product_name] controller and SCADA system are not in the same subnet, you will need a gateway such as a router.
Hi, I would like to suggest a solution if possible. Is any recommendation welcome here? Please let me know which method would be the best.

If your SCADA system can communicate with the [product_name] controller over a LAN, then using a VPN is the simplest way. For more targeted responses, please provide specific questions. Regards, [user_name]

There is currently no setup in place. The project involves connecting between 4 and 25 [product_name] controllers in separate locations to a central monitoring station elsewhere. A SCADA system is one suggestion, but alternative solutions are also welcome.

As [user_name] mentioned, more details would help. Your question is too general. When you mention Ethernet, do you mean a company network, or are these locations far apart, requiring public internet? Also, specifying 4 to 25 [product_name] controllers isn't precise. What do you expect from SCADA—would an HMI suffice, or is something more complex needed? Also keep in mind: this is a user forum, not an official hotline or support center. The platform is provided and monitored by [company_name]. For direct support, please raise a support request or contact your local [company_name] office.

Currently, there is neither hardware, software, nor a defined plan, but you seek guidance on connecting everything. Start by mapping out the existing locations, including internet access details like fixed IP or dynamic DNS. Explain what you want to monitor via SCADA or PC. Using VPNs lets you treat each controller as a local device. You could also use the internal web server or an enhanced server created by [product_name] web editor software, which simplifies monitoring multiple signals. Note that real-time connectivity over the internet is not possible, and sequence data might sometimes be lost. For further guidance, consult manuals for the controller and web editor software. There are no generic solutions suitable for every situation. Regards, [user_name]

Thank you all for your valuable advice. I've attached a project layout to clarify: 1) Four [product_name] controllers are in different locations without LAN connectivity between them. 2) The goal is to monitor both analog and digital signals nearly live (some minor data loss is fine), mostly related to water salinity, and no rapid actions are expected. 3) As outlined, we want to centralize monitoring of these signals from all four controllers at one location, aiming for a cost-effective solution. Do you think the [product_name] web editor software is suitable for this? Also, to avoid using routers with static IPs, can dynamic DNS be used?

You now have an initial project design, but still lack essential details. Since there's no direct connection between the [product_name] controllers and the monitoring station, every site needs an internet connection, usually via a router for each location. If those routers are part of a company network, the network administrator should determine whether VPN connections are permitted. Download the controller and web editor manuals to review the internal and extended web server features. The internal web server can display values and messages, and allows monitoring up to eight variables on a separate page. The extended web server offers more features and custom layouts, needing at least [product_name] V[version_no] and SDCards for each controller. Depending on your needs, you can implement more advanced solutions such as creating your own interface, with clients and servers available online for various programming languages. Start by testing the internal web server locally, then add VPN connectivity for remote access if suitable. Regards, [user_name]

Your technical support is extremely useful—thank you! I have one final question: Is it possible to use public internet connectivity without VPN, if security is not a concern? Referring to the attached image, if that's feasible, which communication processor would you recommend? VPN is available, but I am exploring a more cost-effective alternative.

Direct communication between two LAN networks is not possible—see the 'private networks' section in this [url]. LAN packets need to be encapsulated for WAN transmission, typically using VPN or IP tunneling. Since I'm not a WAN/VPN/IP Tunnel expert, I suggest searching online for further details, beginning with the provided [url]. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are exploring how to remotely monitor multiple [product_name] controllers from diverse sites on a central SCADA system in a cost-efficient way, without an existing network infrastructure or direct LAN links. Discussions cover hardware requirements, available software options, network configurations—including use of VPN, static IP, and dynamic DNS—and feasibility of enhanced visualization and multi-site monitoring via the [product_name] web editor. Users recognize challenges such as limited real-time capability over the internet and some data loss risk, clarifying that their monitoring needs are for near-live data, not urgent control.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to integrate several remote [product_name] controllers into a central monitoring solution that provides timely data and is affordable, with minimal complexity and infrastructure requirements. They are open to different implementation methods and are especially interested in avoiding expensive and intricate setups such as VPN or static IP, if alternatives such as dynamic DNS can work.
